title: approve refuses a caller over ssh
intention: The artifact door's approve refuses any caller that descends from an ssh login, Akien's included, until CC has its own ssh key (outline 17.2.2).
why: Measured 2026-11-18 on akiendelllinux: an ssh login's shell sits in session-4397.scope, which classify() reads as akien, under sshd-session (OpenSSH 10.2p1). CC on akienasus logs in with akien@akienasus, the key Akien's own ssh would use, and its environment does not cross ssh, so CC over ssh is classed akien and can approve a hand edit as him (Q#115, CairnCommons/questions/open-0bfaf0f5aa8b.json). Akien answered 2026-11-18: until CC's key lands, approve and the operator close refuse any sshd-session caller, Akien's included.
traces_to: Law 6: approve is the owner's gate, and a CC classed akien over ssh passes it ambiently. Outline 17.2.2 (-amm).
how: ancestry() records each pid's comm from /proc/<pid>/comm (None when unreadable). caller() sets me['ssh'] = the pid of the first ancestor whose comm is sshd-session or sshd (the older OpenSSH child), only when one is found, so a local caller's journal entry keeps its shape. approve() refuses a caller carrying ssh before its class check, naming the ssh login and Q#115. A red-first proof injects the ancestry with mock.patch.object, as cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_the_caller_reads_whose_terminal_it_is.py does. The trouble device's operator close is a sibling ticket (Q#103).

out: cairn/devices/trouble (the operator close, a sibling ticket)
ticket 62e7bff757c0 (CC's own key) and every other component
